title: o
source:
'''Sesotho word (South African orthography):''' o
'''Sesotho word (Lesotho orthography):''' o


'''English translation:''' ''you'' - singular (subject concord used pronominally)

'''Derivative(s)/Related word(s):''' [[wena]] (''you'' - second person absolute pronoun; singular)
'''Example of usage:''' Wena o motswalle wa ka. ''(You are my friend.)'' ---- '''Sesotho word (South African orthography):''' o
'''Sesotho word (Lesotho orthography):''' o

o - subject concord

In Sesotho nouns are divided into various noun classes. The noun class determines the subject concord for instance - this is very important in the construction of sentences.
Class Prefix Subject 
concord		 Example Translation
of example
1 mo- o mosadi woman
2 ba- ba basadi women
1a - o ntate father
2a ba- ba bontate fathers
3 mo- o mose dress
4 me- e mese dresses
5 le- le leleme tongue
6 ma- a maleme tongues
7 se- se sefate tree
8 di- di difate trees
9 - e ntja dog
10 di- di dintja dogs
Classes 11, 12 and 13 are mainly used in languages such as isiZulu and isiXhosa
14 bo- bo bohobe bread
15 ho- ho ho tsamaja to walk
16 - ho fatshe down
17 ho- ho hodimo up
18 mo- o mose abroad
